_comment: Reviewed corpus-vacuity records for the cross-language artifact-role parity
gate (datrix/scripts/test/artifact-role-parity-gate.ps1). Each entry names one
(language, domain) coordinate where that language declares the domain
'supported' and its declared structural_pattern matches ZERO paths anywhere in
that language's ENTIRE blessed footprint under scripts/config/parity-baselines/.
The gate SKIPS such a domain when comparing role sets -- correctly, since a
single-example 'missing' verdict over a construct no example declares carries no
information. The skip used to be silent, and silence is the defect these records
close: a generator no reference example reaches has no end-to-end signal at all,
and nothing distinguished 'no example CAN reach this' from 'no example HAPPENS
to'. Every skip now carries a status and a reason, and the gate fails on an
unrecorded pair AND on a record whose pair is no longer vacuous.
The three statuses are never interchangeable -- each carries a different remedy:
unreachable-by-design  No reference example can produce a matching file at
all, whatever it declares and whatever it targets;
something outside the example's control gates the
emission. Adding an example is never the remedy.
cloud-platform-only    Reachable only by an example whose deployment profile
resolves to a cloud provider. Every example resolves
provider = "local" (108 declarations across the example
configs; zero aws/azure in any profile of any example),
so this is not a missing DSL block -- it is the corpus
having no cloud-targeting example at all, which would
swap that example's ENTIRE infrastructure output.
unexercised            Reachable under the corpus's own local/docker shape;
no example declares the triggering construct. Ordinary
corpus-coverage debt, closed by one DSL addition.
Never close a record by weakening the language's declaration. Flipping a domain
to 'unsupported' so the census stops seeing it is a false stance, not a fix.
Every reason below was established by reading the gating code and by running the
stated matcher against a known instance first, so an absence count is evidence
rather than a matcher that silently matches nothing.
expected_count is a pinned, reviewed value: change it only in the same change
that adds or removes a record.

records.reason: Pattern */src/*/Infrastructure/*.cs. CDN-module emission requires all three of: the resolved platform realizing CDN cache invalidation, a declared cdn block, and that block enabled (datrix-codegen-common/src/datrix_codegen_common/platform/cdn_emission.py, service_needs_cdn_module). provides_cdn_cache_invalidation is True only on the aws and azure platform capability declarations (datrix-codegen-aws/src/datrix_codegen_aws/plugin/capability.py, datrix-codegen-azure/src/datrix_codegen_azure/plugin/capability.py); azure-vm declares it False and the local docker target does not declare it at all. Both preconditions are missing from the corpus: zero cdn blocks in the 201 example .dtrx files (the matcher finds the cdn-*.dtrx transformer fixtures in datrix-language, so it is not silently matching nothing), and every example config resolves deployment.provider = "local". Closing this needs the corpus's first cloud-targeting example, not a cdn block.

Pattern */src/*/Clients/*Errors.cs -- the per-extern-service errors file the extern-client generator emits alongside its client/models/contracts. No reference example declares an extern service: zero matches across all 201 example .dtrx files, with the same matcher finding the real declarations in datrix-codegen-dotnet/tests/e2e/fixtures/extern-client-wiring/pricing-engine-extern.dtrx and datrix-codegen-typescript/tests/fixtures/system-full-domain-surface.dtrx. Nothing platform-gated stands in the way -- an extern service is wired on the local docker target (compose entry, health check, environment). NOTE for anyone reading the census: this is not a dotnet-only gap. Because no example declares an extern service in ANY language, no language's blessed footprint contains a real extern client. java's, python's and typescript's extern_client patterns used to be broad enough to match neighbouring inter-service client output in the same directory, so those three read as non-vacuous off another domain's files and never reached this file; each is now suffix-scoped to its own models family and carries its own record below.

Pattern */src/*/Migrations/*/*.cs. Every blessed baseline is produced by scripts/library/test/reference_example_parity.py's generate_example, which builds PipelineConfig(target_language=..., profile="test") and so inherits PipelineConfig.migrations = False (datrix-cli/src/datrix_cli/pipeline/contract.py) -- the pipeline's migrations stage never runs on the blessing path, in any language. No DSL an example could declare changes that: the one example config that sets migrations.enabled = true (03-domains/ecommerce, whose test profile inherits that base block) still has no migration artifact in any of its blessed manifests, and the other 53 set it false. The remedy is a decision about whether baselines should be blessed with migrations on -- migration output is schema-delta dependent, which is why the blessing path does not -- never an added example.

Pattern */src/*/Search/*/*.cs. The dotnet search orchestrator gates only on service.search_blocks being non-empty (datrix-codegen-dotnet/src/datrix_codegen_dotnet/generators/persistence/_dotnet_search_orchestrator.py, generate_for_service) -- no platform or provider condition anywhere in the chain -- and the local docker target realizes a search block end-to-end (Elasticsearch cluster plus per-service index-init containers, datrix-codegen-docker/.../compose/_wiring_nosql.py). No reference example declares a search block: zero `search <name> {` matches across all 201 example .dtrx files, with the same matcher finding `search elastic {` in datrix-language's own grammar corpus. dotnet is the only language with a standalone search domain -- python, typescript and java fold search into their already-exercised integration domain -- so this is dotnet's only search coverage signal.

Pattern */src/*/Serverless/*/Handlers/*Handler.cs names the platform-agnostic handler classes DotnetServerlessMicroGen.render emits, and that method returns [] for a CONTAINER-platform block by explicit design (datrix-codegen-dotnet/src/datrix_codegen_dotnet/micro_generators/serverless.py): the container broker entrypoints carry each transpiled body inline, so emitting handler classes as well would duplicate the same DSL body with the second copy referenced by nothing. The serverless platform is a pure function of the deployment provider (datrix-common/src/datrix_common/config/serverless/hosting_validation.py, derive_serverless_platform: aws -> lambda, azure -> functions, local -> container), and every example resolves provider = "local". Unlike the other cloud-only entries this domain is NOT without corpus signal: the serverless example's dotnet baseline pins the CONTAINER realization under Serverless/{Block}/ (IngestionHandlersContainerConsumer.cs, QueueWorkersContainerQueueWorker.cs, DailyOrderReportJob.cs), and the LAMBDA path carries its own package-level coverage in datrix-codegen-dotnet/tests/integration/test_lambda_serverless_pipeline.py. A contrived example is not warranted; only the corpus's cloud-example decision would make this pattern match.

Pattern */src/*/SoftDelete/*/*.cs names the soft-delete CASCADE file family, which is driven by the onSoftDelete relationship modifier (datrix-common/src/datrix_common/datrix_model/entity.py, Relationship.has_soft_delete_cascade -> has_modifier("onSoftDelete"); consumed by build_soft_delete_cascades in datrix-codegen-common/src/datrix_codegen_common/algorithms/entity_relationships.py). The corpus DOES exercise the SoftDeletable trait -- 31 declarations across the example .dtrx files -- but declares the onSoftDelete modifier zero times, and the same matcher finds it in datrix-codegen-dotnet/tests/e2e/fixtures/combined-surface/ and datrix-codegen-java/tests/fixtures/audit-soft-delete-entities.dtrx. The remedy is one `: onSoftDelete` modifier on an existing hasMany between two entities that already carry `with SoftDeletable`; no platform dependency.
